title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: 1. The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment (MOEWOE) has developed ‘Action Plan (2021-2025) of the 8th Five Year Plan on Overseas Employment and Well-being of Migrant Workers’ in December 2022 and started implementing the action plan since December 2022. The plan commits the government to establishing fair recruitment, skill development and protection of migrant workers in line with International Labour Standards, and to working through tripartite social dialogue. 2. The Government of Bangladesh (MOEWOE) has drafted and validated the Reintegration Policy for migrant workers from February 2022 to April 2023 which is now under the process of cabinet approval. The policy covers overarching directives for reintegration (including returnee database and one-stop centres), social reintegration of returnee migrants (including universal social protection), economic reintegration of returnee migrants (including active labour market policies), physical and psychosocial well-being of returnees and their family members and effective coordination and management of the reintegration process. 3. The Government of Bangladesh (MOEWOE) has gazetted Wage Earners’ Welfare Board rule in April 2023 strengthening reintegration services and access to justice for returning migrant workers. 4. The MOEWOE adopted the unified pre-departure orientation module for outgoing migrant workers in November 2022. 5. For the first time, the GOB has introduced labour migration module related to the cost of migration in the Labour Force Survey 2022 addressing SDG target 10.7.1. 1.1 With the support of the Government of Switzerland, ILO acted as a member secretary of the technical working committee to develop the action plan during March- December 2022. 1.2 ILO conducted 13 meetings of the technical working committee including MOEWOE, Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET), Wage Earners’ Welfare Board (WEWB), Probashi Kallyan Bank (PKB) and Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL) during March- December 2022 1.3 ILO conducted one validation workshop of the draft action plan on 30 August 2022 with more than 80 officials of tripartite plus constituents. 1.4 ILO has supported the printing and dissemination of 600 copies of the action plan to relevant stakeholders and also supported the orientation of 25 officials of MOE, BMET, WEWB, PKB, and BOESL to implement and reporting of the action plan. 2.1 ILO acted as a member secretary for the technical working committee to support the development of the draft policy from February 2022 to April 2023. 2.2 ILO in collaboration with IOM and UN Women conducted 16 meetings of the technical committee to develop the draft of the reintegration policy. 2.3 ILO supported two national consultations on 27 February and 22 March 2022 and one validation workshop on 31 March 2022 of the draft reintegration policy. 3.1 ILO acted as the member secretary for WEWB rule development technical committee as member secretary. Eleven consultation meetings with tripartite plus constituents to develop the WEWB rule and drafting of the rule took place between January 2022 to December 2022. 4.1 ILO has supported developing the unified pre-departure orientation module for outgoing migrant workers through eight bilateral meetings and two technical workshops. 5.1 ILO supported BBS in the development of labour migration module related to cost of migration for the labour force survey through a series of consultation meetings with relevant stakeholders.

description.narrative: Bangladesh has adopted a digital recruitment monitoring platform: the Recruiting Agents’ Information Management System (RAIMS), operated by the Bangladeshi Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) since 2022 to create a more transparent recruitment and recruitment monitoring process with greater oversight of recruitment agencies. During the reporting period, the system received 1324 applications from among the 1527 recruitment agencies. The information archives and change management of the system can be tracked with a particular user tracking system. The system provides easy access for searching information of any recruiting agents with a dynamic and customized reporting system, including information on grievances raised against the recruiter. RAIMS also provides the necessary data for performance management and classification of recruiting agents. The user notification system helps the BMET and recruiting agents to communicate between both parties. 15 labour attaché had capacities built through three-day training and 11 labour attaché through one-day training on labour migration, BLA MOU, ILS, social protection, fair recruitment and skills development before their placement at the country of destination which built their capacity to enhance their consular services for the migrant workers of Bangladesh. With the support of the Government of Switzerland ILO supported the development of the software and operation manual of the Recruiting Agents’ Information Management System (RAIMS) and conducted capacity development of 20 staff of BMET on the use of RAIMS. ILO provided three days of training to 15 labour attaché and one-day training to 11 labour attaches on labour migration, BLA MOU, ILS, social protection, fair recruitment and skills development before their placement at the country of destination (11-13 February 2022; 14 June 2023).
